<message t="18:42" d="18.03" type="audio">Let me share - I have the files ready here. I can walk you through what I was thinking with the morning shots at the cooperative. The light was... franchement, it was perfect that hour.</message>

</turn>

<turn>
<state>
footage review; 4 turns remaining; project timeline

<message t="18:44" d="18.03" type="audio">Okay okay I'm sharing now - you should see my screen</message>
<message t="18:45" d="18.03" type="audio">So this is exactly what I wanted to show you. The cooperative thing - I thought about what you said in the brief, about moving past the aesthetic shots. These women, they've been doing this work for forty years, some of them. The hands tell the story.</message>
<message t="18:46" d="18.03" type="audio">See here - I caught the morning light through the window while she's crushing the kernels. No artificial anything. Just... *hammam* light, you know? Like soft and real.</message>
</turn>

<turn>
<state>
footage review; 3 turns remaining; project timeline
</state>
<message t="18:46" d="18.03" type="audio">Sorry I just - can you go back three seconds? My wifi stuttered.</message>
<message t="18:47" d="18.03" type="audio">Okay yes. I see it now. The way the dust catches the light when she - that's... that's exactly what I hoped for when I wrote "documentary feel" in the brief but I didn't know if I was explaining it right.</message>
<message t="18:48" d="18.03" type="audio">You captured something real here. The hands especially. We have all this glossy content of, you know, perfectly poured lattes and clean white counters. But this has weight to it. History.</message>
</turn>

<turn>
<state>
footage review; 2 turns remaining; project timeline
</state>
<message t="18:48" d="18.03" type="audio">Honestly when you said documentary feel in the brief, I thought about my grandmother. She used to do this work, the argan, before her hands got - you know, tired. So I knew exactly what you meant.</message>
<message t="18:49" d="18.03" type="audio">The women at the cooperative, they let me stay for two hours. I think they thought I was crazy, crouching in corners with my camera. But one of them - Hajja Fatima, she's seventy-three - she kept looking at the lens and laughing.</message>
<message t="18:50" d="18.03" type="audio">Here, let me skip ahead. There's a shot I want you to see. The sorting table. It's less... poetic, maybe. But I think it matters for the full picture.</message>
</turn>

<turn>
<state>
footage review; 1 turns remaining; project timeline
</state>
<message t="18:50" d="18.03" type="audio">Your grandmother did this work?</message>
<message t="18:51" d="18.03" type="audio">Sorry I just - that's not what I expected you to say. I wrote those bullet points on a brief at 11 PM staring at a candle because the power was out and I was eating cold pasta and now there's a seventy-three year old woman named Hajja Fatima laughing at your camera and your grandmother's hands in my head and I don't know, it feels like a lot for a coffee brand's Instagram content, but - in a good way?</message>
<message t="18:52" d="18.03" type="audio">Show me the sorting table. I want to see everything.</message>
</turn>

<turn>
<state>
project timeline; 5 turns remaining; payment logistics
</state>
<message t="18:52" d="18.03" type="audio">Okay - here. The sorting table.</message>
<message t="18:53" d="18.03" type="audio">You'll see it's less... cinematic, I guess? But I kept thinking about what you said. "Documentary feel." This is the unsexy part. The kernels that don't make the cut. The hands moving through them fast, you know, sorting the good from the broken. It's repetitive. It's work.</message>
<message t="18:54" d="18.03" type="audio">I have maybe forty minutes total from the cooperative. And then the café footage from Agadir - the new place near the marina. That's another hour or so raw. If this is working for you, I can start cutting the first deliverable by end of week.</message>
</turn>

<turn>
<state>
project timeline; 4 turns remaining; payment logistics
</state>
<message t="18:54" d="18.03" type="audio">No I - the unsexy part is exactly right. That's what I meant about weight. Anyone can film a pretty latte. Not everyone thinks to show the sorting, the... the rejection. That's where the story is.</message>
<message t="18:55" d="18.03" type="audio">End of week for first cut works. My boss has been asking about the series launch date and I've been, you know, creatively avoiding giving him one.</message>
<message t="18:55" d="18.03" type="audio">What's your process look like for revisions? I want to make sure I'm not that client who asks for seventeen small tweaks when you're trying to move on to the next thing.</message>
</turn>

<turn>
<state>
project timeline; 3 turns remaining; payment logistics
</state>
<message t="18:56" d="18.03" type="audio">Honestly? I'm used to the tourism clients. The ones who want "more blue" or "can you make it feel more Moroccan but not too Moroccan" - you know the type. So I built a process for that.</message>
<message t="18:56" d="18.03" type="audio">What I usually do is - I send you a rough cut, you give me notes in one go if possible. Bullet points, voice notes, whatever works. And I turn it around in forty-eight hours. After that, if there's small stuff, fine, but I try to get most of it right on the first revision, you know?</message>
<message t="18:57" d="18.03" type="audio">The key thing for me is - don't be polite. If something doesn't work, tell me directly. I can take it wallah. I'd rather you say "this transition feels weird" than have you show it to your boss and feel unsure about it.</message>
</turn>

<turn>
<state>
project timeline; 2 turns remaining; payment logistics
</state>
<instant_event>
A boy - sixteen, seventeen? - same eyes as Saad. Curtain swinging behind him. The space beyond not a separate room, just a corner. A bedframe. Textbooks. This is his sister's bed he's sitting on, he said - law textbooks. How many people in that space? The charger grabbed, the boy gone. Saad's hand still raised from waving him off. The apology already forming.
</instant_event>
<message t="18:57" d="18.03" type="audio">No I appreciate that, the direct thing. I'll try not to be - you know, Ukrainian polite about it. We have this thing where we say "maybe we could possibly consider" when we mean "no, absolutely not."</message>
<message t="18:58" d="18.03" type="audio">Your brother seems like he was on a mission.</message>
<message t="18:58" d="18.03" type="audio">Sorry - I know that's not what we're here to discuss. I just... you mentioned your sister's textbooks before, and now there's a brother, and I'm sitting in my rented studio that's basically one room with a hot plate, and I don't know why I'm telling you this except that it feels strange to only talk about deliverables when we've already talked about your grandmother's hands.</message>
</turn>

<turn>
<state>
payment logistics; 3 turns remaining
</state>
<message t="18:59" d="18.03" type="audio">That's Amine. Sixteen years old and he thinks the charger belongs to whoever grabs it first wallah. We share that room - me, him, and a curtain that doesn't quite close all the way.</message>
<message t="19:00" d="18.03" type="audio">You know I've spent three years on these calls trying to look like I have a proper office setup. And then he walks through and - well. There's the reality. Four people in that apartment. But maybe the real thing is better? That's what made the cooperative footage work anyway.</message>
<message t="19:01" d="18.03" type="audio">Anyway - I should ask about payment logistics while we're talking. I know Upwork handles the contract side but is there anything specific your company needs from me for their records? Invoice format, whatever. I want to make sure I'm set up correctly on your end.</message>
</turn>

<turn>
<state>
payment logistics; 2 turns remaining
</state>
<message t="19:02" d="18.03" type="audio">Our finance situation is - okay, honestly it's my boss's wife. She handles the books from their kitchen table. So whatever Upwork auto-generates for invoices, that should be fine. She just needs something to print for the tax records.</message>
<message t="19:03" d="18.03" type="audio">If there's anything specific on your end - like, I know some freelancers need payment in a certain timeframe for currency reasons - you can write it into the next deliverable notes. We've never hired someone outside Ukraine before so I'm probably forgetting something.</message>
<message t="19:04" d="18.03" type="audio">Four people in that apartment. And here I thought my five plants made my studio crowded.</message>
</turn>

<turn>
<state>
payment logistics; 1 turns remaining
</state>
<message t="19:04" d="18.03" type="audio">Five plants! Okay, that's a whole ecosystem. You're running a botanical garden over there.</message>
<message t="19:05" d="18.03" type="audio">No, seriously - the Upwork system works for me. I've had clients delay payments before, the ones who say "net-30" and mean "whenever we remember," but your setup sounds fine. As long as the platform releases it within a week of delivery, I can plan around that.</message>
<message t="19:06" d="18.03" type="audio">The currency thing - honestly, dirham is stable enough for now. I'm not going to complicate it. Just whatever the standard conversion is on payment day. I've learned not to stress about rates I can't control wallah.</message>
</turn>

<turn>
<state>
predefined_topics_exhausted
</state>
<message t="19:06" d="18.03" type="audio">I like that you say wallah. I don't know why, it just - it sounds like you mean it. When I say truly at the end of sentences it's the same thing I think. My mother hates it, says I picked it up from the internet.</message>
<message t="19:07" d="18.03" type="audio">Anyway. Yes. Payment settled, revision process settled, footage is - honestly better than I expected. You should send me the invoice whenever you're ready and I'll make sure it doesn't get lost in the kitchen table system.</message>
<message t="19:08" d="18.03" type="audio">I know we said we'd keep this professional but... I'm glad we did the video call. Seventeen text bubbles didn't tell me you have a brother who steals chargers. Or that your grandmother's hands are in this project too.</message>
<message t="19:09" d="18.03" type="audio">End of week for the first cut. And Saad - thank you. For catching that light. For the unsexy sorting table. It matters more than I can explain to my boss who just wants engagement metrics, but... I'll figure out how to make him see it.</message>
</turn>

<turn>
<state>
predefined_topics_exhausted
</state>
<message t="19:10" d="18.03" type="audio">Your mother thinks you picked up truly from the internet? Tell her it's wisdom wallah. The internet is not always wrong.</message>
<message t="19:11" d="18.03" type="audio">But honestly - thank you for saying that. About the hands. About the project having weight. Most clients just want the content to fill a calendar. They don't think about what's behind it. You wrote a brief about coffee culture and now you're thinking about grandmothers and sorting tables and - I don't know. That's the good part of this work. When it becomes something real.</message>
<message t="19:12" d="18.03" type="audio">End of week. First cut in your inbox. And Olena - next time you're eating cold pasta by candlelight, just remember there's a guy in Inezgane very seriously filming argan kernels at 6 AM for you.</message>
</turn>

<turn>
<state>
<predefined_topics_exhausted/>
</state>
<message t="19:12" d="18.03" type="audio">I'm going to screenshot that sentence and look at it during my next 3 AM anxiety spiral. A guy in Inezgane, very seriously filming kernels. Somehow that helps.</message>
<message t="19:13" d="18.03" type="audio">It's late there too - later for you, actually. I should let you go. Your whole family is probably wondering why you've been talking to your screen for half an hour.</message>
<message t="19:14" d="18.03" type="audio">This was good, Saad. I'll send you the brand guidelines document tomorrow - the real one, not the one I wrote by candlelight. And we'll talk soon.</message>
<message t="19:14" d="18.03" type="audio">Take care of those hands. Yours, I mean. Not just your grandmother's.</message>
</turn>
